transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um, so... I guess I'm here because of my eating. It's just getting really weird. Like, what really made me come in is that once I start eating like that, it feels like I hit some switch, you know? And I just keep going even while part of me is thinking, *Dennis, just stop already*. 

But I don't. Which is frustrating because I never used to be like this. Like, back when I was actually taking classes—I'm taking a semester off from college right now, just to figure things out, because honestly, the whole online portal thing they use for assignments was just constantly crashing on me. My laptop is so old it barely runs it anyway, it's basically a brick at this point. I really need to get a new one, but I'm not working right now, so money's kind of tight and I can't exactly afford a Mac or anything. My roommate has one and it's so much faster. 

But yeah, anyway, the whole not being able to stop eating thing... that's why I made the appointment.
When you say you can't stop eating once you start, does this usually happen in episodes where you end up eating a lot more than most people would in a similar time period?

Yeah, um, definitely. It's... it's a lot. Like, especially on nights after a project deadline, or if there's just leftover pizza hanging around the apartment. I'll end up taking it to my room and eating a whole small pizza, plus a bunch of chips, and then cereal on top of that... just way more than I ever planned to, and definitely way more than my roommates would ever eat for a normal dinner. 

But my roommates are the ones who always order it, and they get it from that place on 4th street with the super thick crust. I don't even really like thick crust, honestly, it's just too doughy. I usually buy the frozen thin crust ones from the grocery store. But they just leave the cardboard boxes sitting out on the kitchen counter instead of taking out the trash. It drives me completely crazy because last summer we got ants because of that. The landlord took like three weeks to send an exterminator, and he's this really grumpy guy who never answers his phone, so I had to keep going down to his office... but yeah, anyway, I just end up eating all of it.
When you're eating all of that in one sitting, does it feel like you're not in control of yourself, like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah, exactly. That's... that's exactly it. Like I said before, it's like I hit a switch or something. I'll be sitting there, eating, and there's this voice in my head going, *Dennis, just stop already, you don't need another slice*, but my hands just keep moving. It's like I'm watching myself do it but I can't actually make myself stop. 

Which is weird, because I'm usually pretty good at controlling things. Like when I used to play baseball in high school. I was a pitcher, right? You have to have so much control. My coach, Mr. Henderson, he used to make us do these crazy focus drills where we had to stare at a spot on the wall for like five minutes without blinking. He was super intense. He actually got fired my senior year because he yelled at a referee during a playoff game and threw a cooler of Gatorade. It got all over the assistant coach, who was wearing these really expensive khakis. I always wondered how he got the stain out, or if he just threw them away. Khakis are so hard to keep clean anyway, which is why I mostly just wear jeans... but yeah, I just feel totally out of control when the eating starts.
Do these eating episodes make you feel really upset, guilty, or interfere with your daily life, like your schoolwork or relationships with others?

Yeah, I mean... it definitely makes me upset. Like, I'm still making it to my classes—well, when I was taking them before this semester off—and my robotics club meetings. I still go to those. But the morning after I eat like that, I just feel so sluggish and distracted. And I spend way too much time worrying if my roommates noticed the missing food or the wrappers in the trash. 

Which is annoying because our trash can is one of those motion-sensor ones, you know? You just wave your hand over it and it opens. My mom bought it for us when we moved in because she's obsessed with germs. She won't even touch door handles in public restrooms, she uses a paper towel every time. And if there are no paper towels, she'll use her sleeve, which I think kind of defeats the purpose because then the germs are just on your clothes, right? And she washes her clothes in this weird eco-friendly detergent that smells like pine needles. I hate the smell of pine. It reminds me of those little tree air fresheners people hang in their cars. My uncle had one in his truck, and his truck always smelled like wet dog and fake pine... 

But yeah, anyway, the eating thing... it bothers me a lot, but it hasn't completely knocked me off track or ruined my life or anything. It's just really frustrating to deal with.
